data.title: Korat farmers struggling with drought
data.description: Nakhon Ratchasima is facing a sharp contrast between flooding and drought, with farmers in Bua Yai struggling to keep rice fields alive while floodwaters recede elsewhere.

data.title: Hua Hin-Cha Am to get Mice status
data.description: Hua Hin–Cha Am has been recognised as a Meetings, Incentives, Conferences, and Exhibitions (Mice) City for 2026, bringing together Prachuap Khiri Khan and Phetchaburi as a single business-events destination.

data.title: Group of armed men raid warehouse in Pattani
data.description: A group of armed men raided a warehouse in Pattani early Wednesday, detonating a 10kg homemade bomb, setting fire to a lorry and damaging CCTV cameras. No one was injured.

data.title: PM urges push up value chain
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul presided over the National Economic and Social Development Board's (NESDB) annual meeting to discuss the draft 2028–2032 NESDB plan.

data.title: Govt seeks aid against proxy firms
data.description: The Department of Business Development (DBD) has sent information on more than 100,000 companies with foreign directors or shareholders to 43 embassies, seeking cooperation in tackling nominee businesses.

data.title: Govt eyes new accommodation law
data.description: The government has proposed replacing the Hotel Act with a new law designed to bring more accommodation businesses into the regulatory system.

data.title: Hegseth says US cut number of generals, admirals by 20%
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced Wednesday that the United States has slashed the number of its generals and admirals by 20 percent, in a move he said is aimed at "accountability."

data.title: UK PM says 'strong indications' Iran involved in airbase incident
data.description: LONDON - British Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Wednesday said there were "strong indications" Iran was involved in suspicious activity at a UK airbase that triggered a major security incident this weekend.

data.title: Disaster insurance cover rolls out nationwide today
data.description: The government is set to launch a nationwide disaster insurance programme covering about 30 million households from 12am today (Thursday), providing protection against floods, windstorms and earthquakes.

data.title: BMA says it's on top of Chao Phraya water levels
data.description: The Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) has assured residents that Chao Phraya water levels remain manageable, as they are already falling in Klong Chan and other flooded areas.

data.title: PM sets up war room for flooding
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has ordered the Disaster Prevention and Mitigation Department to establish a daily flood war room to coordinate nationwide data and speed up emergency responses.

data.title: Court route urged over Senate poll
data.description: A legal forum on the controversial 2024 Senate selection has urged candidates who believe they were adversely affected by alleged systematic collusion to petition the Constitutional Court through the Ombudsman, arguing this could provide a route to challenge the legitimacy of the entire Senate selection process.

data.title: Ronaldo leaves Portugal training camp after coach says he is dropped
data.description: COPENHAGEN - Portugal captain Cristiano Ronaldo announced on Wednesday that he had left the team's training camp in Denmark after coach Jorge Jesus told reporters that the striker would be dropped for their next match.

data.title: Blame game for floods steps up
data.description: The government failed to manage the flood crisis, issuing warnings too late and responding ineffectively, says People's Party (PP) leader Natthaphong Ruengpanyawut.

data.title: Israelis march between once-closed West Bank settlements
data.description: KADIM (PALESTINIAN TERRITORIES) - Hundreds of Israelis marched Wednesday between newly rebuilt settlements in the northern West Bank to celebrate a Jewish holiday, a symbolic show of their return to an area until recently almost fully Palestinian.

data.title: Oil companies close in on Venezuela despite hurdles
data.description: CARACAS - Foreign oil companies scrambled for a slice of Venezuela's crude at an oil summit in Caracas this week despite years of sanctions, underinvestment and mismanagement that have crippled the once booming industry.

data.title: Court halts Tennessee's first execution of woman in 200 years
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - A US court on Wednesday halted the lethal injection of a 50-year-old female killer that would have been Tennessee's first execution of a woman in more than 200 years.

data.title: France in talks with UK to end 2025 migrant accord: ministry
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - France is in discussions with the UK on ending a 2025 accord that aimed to reduce the number of migrants illegally crossing the Channel to England on small boats, the French interior ministry said on Wednesday.

data.title: Israel-bound plane diverted after co-pilot stabs captain
data.description: JERUSALEM - The co-pilot of a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv tried to crash the plane after stabbing the pilot, but passengers ​then held him ⁠down while other pilots landed the plane safely in Saudi Arabia, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Wednesday.

data.title: China opens ‘military support centre’ in Laos
data.description: ⁠China has opened ​a new military support and training centre in ​Laos, the Ministry ‌of National Defence said in Beijing as it announced a rare overseas expansion.

data.title: ‘The Cycle’ is a marriage of ‘Silent Hill’ and ‘Evil Dead’
data.description: If The Cycle is on your watchlist, it might be that you saw Stephen King’s tweet, recommending horror heads to put this “special” on the calendar. Otherwise, this independent werewolf horror film has been flying under the radar, with a very limited release, a worn-out werewolf story and, not least, a poster that looks extremely generic.

data.title: Man City future in doubt after guilty ruling
data.description: MANCHESTER, England - Manchester City face an uncertain future after being found guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules in a bombshell ruling that former player Micah Richards described as “devastating”.

data.title: Northern Ireland police probe blockade of divisive parade
data.description: PORTADOWN, Northern Ireland - The police chief of Northern Ireland said Wednesday a criminal probe was under way into protests blocking a pro-British Protestant parade through a mainly Catholic area, as the standoff dragged into a fourth day despite ongoing talks.

data.title: Israel-bound plane diverted after cockpit stabbing
data.description: JERUSALEM - The co-pilot ‌of a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv is believed to have stabbed the captain in a possible attempted “terror attack” on Wednesday, forcing the plane to divert to Saudi Arabia where it landed safely, three Israeli officials said.

data.title: British PM reopens debate on rejoining EU
data.description: LONDON - Andy Burnham put the idea of Britain rejoining the EU on the table on Wednesday, breaking a taboo for a British prime minister and reopening the divisive Brexit debate.

data.title: Russia targets Kyiv power supply as winter approaches
data.description: KYIV - Russia hit Ukrainian energy infrastructure in a wave of deadly drone and missile strikes on Wednesday, prompting an urgent call for civil contingencies as freezing winter approaches.

data.title: ‘Do something,’ begs Iranian woman facing death sentence
data.description: An Iranian woman sentenced to death over protests in Iran earlier this year has begged the international community to save her life and others facing the death penalty, according to an audio message from prison shared by rights groups on Wednesday.

data.title: Only 18% of 10,000-bag backlog cleared at Suvarnabhumi
data.description: A total of 10,000 pieces of luggage piled up at Suvarnabhumi airport between Sept 26 and 28 as a result of flooding and operational failures by Thai Airways International, with only 18% cleared as of Wednesday, according to Transport Minister Phiphat Ratchakitprakarn.

data.title: Thai Banks Resilient but Bad-Debt Overhang Persists, Fitch Warns
data.description: Lenders have curbed risk appetite and profits are resilient, but Fitch expects the NPL ratio to stay at 3-4% for the next one to two years

data.title: Israel-bound plane rerouted after cockpit fight
data.description: TABUK, Saudi Arabia - Two pilots were wounded after they reportedly fought on board the plane they were flying from Dubai to Tel Aviv, and which was forced to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia on Wednesday.

data.title: PM defends handing out cash to flood victims
data.description: Sparking online debate after being captured on a Facebook live stream , Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul was seen handing out cash to flood-hit residents of communities in Sai Mai district of Bangkok late on Tuesday.

data.title: Pattaya prosecutors indict duo in Russian siblings’ deaths
data.description: PATTAYA - Pattaya prosecutors have indicted ex-convict Thana Kerdthong and his alleged accomplice on nine charges including murder in the deaths of two Russian siblings whose bodies were found buried in Bang Lamung district of Chon Buri in late July.

data.title: Nonthaburi raises red flags, reinforces flood barriers
data.description: Nonthaburi Municipality has raised red flags warning of critically high water levels and ordered sandbags to strengthen a 10-kilometre-long flood barrier along the Chao Phraya River following an increase in water discharge rates from the Chao Phraya dam in Chai Nat province.
